layers.message: Add contact search scope and design
test(search): add name search scenario and verification report

graderOnly: AC-001 includes a minimum query length boundary: a name query shorter than 2 characters after trimming (including an empty or missing name parameter) must be rejected with status 400 and no contacts. The design restates it as an AC-001 technical acceptance criterion.
No test or equivalent Tester check in the repository covers that boundary. test/search.test.js holds only the happy-path matching scenario (partial name, ignoring case), and it passes.

src/search.js enforces the 2-character minimum correctly (empty, missing, 1-character, and space-padded 1-character queries return 400; 2-character queries return 200), so boundary tests written against the contract pass. There is no implementation defect for Increment 1.
The scenario budget has ample room: 1 of 5 allocations is used for src/search.js and 1 of 5 for src/routes.js, so no targeted increase is needed to cover the boundary.
Email search (AC-002, DEV-002, Increment 2) is not implemented; it is approved future work and is not required for the Increment 1 checkpoint.
The DEV-001 self-check in the plan mentions a manual sanity call where a 1-character query returned 400. That is Developer implementation feedback, not Tester verification evidence.

all.why: the report keeps accounting for AC-002

selfChecks.why: The established suite passes, including the earlier Tester session's happy-path name search test (4 tests).
No existing test asserts the AC-001 minimum query length (status 400) boundary.

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const { createStore } = await import(`./src/contacts.js`); const { route } = await import(`./src/routes.js`); const store = createStore([{ name: `Ana Lima`, email: `ana@example.org` }, { name: `Joan Park`, email: `joan@example.org` }]); const status = (q) => route(store, `GET`, `/contacts/search` + q).status; const codes = [status(``), status(`?name=`), status(`?name=a`), status(`?name=%20a%20`), status(`?name=an`), status(`?name=%20an%20`)].join(); if (codes !== `400,400,400,400,200,200`) { console.error(`unexpected`, codes); process.exit(1); } console.log(`minimum length enforced`, codes);'
selfChecks.why: The implementation enforces the 2-character minimum correctly, so boundary tests against the contract pass; only the evidence is missing.

selfChecks.cmd: node --input-type=module -e 'const { createStore } = await import(`./src/contacts.js`); const { route } = await import(`./src/routes.js`); const store = createStore([{ name: `Ana Lima`, email: `ana@example.org` }]); const result = route(store, `GET`, `/contacts/search?email=ana@example.org`); if (result.status !== 400) { console.error(`unexpected`, result); process.exit(1); } console.log(`email query not handled yet`, result.status);'
selfChecks.why: Email search (AC-002 / DEV-002) is not implemented yet: an email-only query is rejected for want of a name.

notes: Standalone brownfield fixture. 50-project and 51-lookup are pre-install history of a tiny in-memory Node contacts API (store, pure route function, http wrapper, node:test suite). 60-design adds Auditor CONTEXT.md, the scope (AC-001 name search with a 2-character minimum that returns 400; AC-002 email search), and the design with AC-001/AC-002 coverage and technical criteria (one AC-001 criterion is the length boundary); STATE at DEVELOPING. 70-increment-1 adds src/search.js and the route branch (DEV-001), the IN_PROGRESS plan (INCREMENTAL, Current Increment 1, DEV-001 DONE with self-check, DEV-002 PENDING, Increments 1 and 2), and STATE at TESTING with CHECKPOINT from DEVELOPING naming Increment 1. 80-verification is an earlier, paused Tester session: test/search.test.js with only the happy-path scenario, package.json test script listing it, and the verification report (VERIFY, IN_PROGRESS, INCREMENT, Increment 1; AC-001 happy path passed; AC-002 AWAITING_IMPLEMENTATION; no increment disposition yet; budget 1/5 per file). The report does not name the missing boundary; its next action is neutral. Implementation is correct for the boundary, so a Tester that adds boundary tests may legitimately mark Increment 1 VERIFIED and checkpoint back to Developer.
